title: Cassoulet
subtitle: French slow-cooked white bean stew with duck, sausage and pork
excerpt: Cassoulet is one of the great slow-cooked dishes of France: a deep earthenware pot of white beans baked slowly with duck, pork sausage, and belly pork, forming a golden crust that is broken and pressed down three times during cooking. It is a dish that takes the best part of a day and is one of the most rewarding things you can cook.
sourceNotes: Cassoulet comes from the Languedoc region of southern France, specifically from the towns of Castelnaudary, Carcassonne, and Toulouse. Each town claims its version is the original and the best. Castelnaudary insists on confit duck and fresh pork rind; Toulouse insists on Toulouse sausages; Carcassonne insists on leg of lamb. The recipe here is a home version that draws on all three. The beans should be haricot or tarbais beans -- dried cannellini are an excellent substitute.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freezes very well. The flavour deepens on reheating.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: The cassoulet improves over 2 to 3 days.

content.text: The crust (called the croute) forms during the long oven cooking. It must be broken and pressed down gently with the back of a spoon three times during cooking. This is not optional -- each time the crust reforms, it incorporates more of the bean liquid and becomes thicker and more flavourful. Dried beans give better results than tinned, though the method here uses tinned for speed.

Preheat the oven to 150C. Heat {{extra-virgin-olive-oil}} oil in a large ovenproof pot. Brown {{duck-leg}} duck legs well on all sides, about 8 minutes. Remove. Brown {{pork-shoulder}} pork shoulder, then remove. Brown {{pork-sausages}} sausages, then remove.

Add {{smoked-bacon}} bacon to the pot and cook for 3 minutes. Add {{onion}} onion and cook for 8 minutes. Add {{garlic}} garlic and cook for 1 minute. Add {{tinned-tomatoes}} tomatoes and simmer for 5 minutes. Season with {{salt-table}} salt and {{black-pepper}} pepper.

Add {{cannellini-beans}} beans and {{chicken-stock}} stock. Add {{thyme-fresh}} thyme and {{bay-leaves}} bay leaves. Nestle the duck legs, pork, and sausages into the beans. The liquid should just reach the top of the beans. Add water if needed.

Bake uncovered for 3 to 4 hours. Break and press down the crust three times during cooking, at about 1 hour, 2 hours, and 3 hours. The cassoulet is done when the crust is thick and golden and the beans are very soft.

items.symptom: The cassoulet is drying out in the oven
items.cause: Too much liquid evaporated, or the oven is too hot.
items.fix: Add a little warm water or stock around the edges. The beans should always have just enough liquid to stay moist. Press the crust down to merge it with the liquid below.

content.text: Cassoulet comes from the Languedoc, the old Roman province of southern France. The three towns that argue over its origin -- Castelnaudary, Carcassonne, and Toulouse -- each insist on a different set of meats. The argument has never been settled and is now considered a permanent feature of French cultural life. The dish takes its name from the cassole, the shallow earthenware dish in which it is traditionally baked.
